name: MIRA
description: The MIRA Surgical System (Miniaturized In Vivo Robotic Assistant) is a compact, portable robotic-assisted surgery platform developed by Virtual Incision Corporation. Unlike traditional multi-hundred-kilogram mainframe surgical robots, MIRA is a ~2-pound in-vivo robotic device designed for tray-to-table setup. Inserted through a single small umbilical incision, MIRA achieves internal triangulation with two articulating wristed instrument arms and a central camera, eliminating external robotic arm clashes and enabling multi-quadrant abdominal access. The surgeon console integrates dual Force Dimension sigma.7 parallel-kinematic haptic master controllers for 7-DOF telemanipulation. A modified research variant (spaceMIRA) was operated aboard the International Space Station in February 2024 as the first surgical robot in space.
